cards.back:
Port 80 (TCP)

HyperText Transfer Protocol — unencrypted web traffic.

Port 443 (TCP)

HTTP Secure — encrypted with TLS/SSL.

Port 53 (UDP for queries, TCP for zone transfers)

Domain Name System — resolves hostnames to IP addresses.

Port 67 (server) and Port 68 (client) — UDP

Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol — assigns IP addresses automatically.

Port 22 (TCP)

Secure Shell — encrypted remote terminal access and file transfer.

Port 20 (data transfer) and Port 21 (control) — TCP

File Transfer Protocol — unencrypted file transfer.

Port 23 (TCP)

Telnet — unencrypted remote terminal access. Replaced by SSH for security.

Port 25 (TCP) — server-to-server email transfer
Port 587 (TCP) — client submission (modern)

Simple Mail Transfer Protocol — sends email.

Port 110 (TCP) — unencrypted
Port 995 (TCP) — POP3 over TLS

Post Office Protocol v3 — downloads email from server (removes from server).

Port 143 (TCP) — unencrypted
Port 993 (TCP) — IMAP over TLS

Internet Message Access Protocol — syncs email (leaves on server).

Port 161 (UDP) — SNMP queries
Port 162 (UDP) — SNMP traps (alerts)

Simple Network Management Protocol — monitors and manages network devices.

Port 3389 (TCP)

Remote Desktop Protocol — Windows GUI remote access. Should be secured with VPN or NLA.

Port 123 (UDP)

Network Time Protocol — synchronizes clocks across network devices. Critical for certificate validation and logging.

Port 389 (TCP/UDP) — unencrypted
Port 636 (TCP) — LDAPS (LDAP over TLS)

Lightweight Directory Access Protocol — used to query Active Directory and other directory services.

Port 445 (TCP)

Server Message Block — Windows file sharing, printer sharing. Also used by ransomware (EternalBlue/WannaCry targeted this port).

Port 179 (TCP)

Border Gateway Protocol — the routing protocol of the internet. Used between autonomous systems (ISPs, large organizations).

Port 22 (TCP) — same as SSH

SSH File Transfer Protocol — secure file transfer over SSH. Not the same as FTPS.

Port 5060 (TCP/UDP) — unencrypted
Port 5061 (TCP) — SIP over TLS

Session Initiation Protocol — sets up VoIP calls. Used with RTP for actual audio.
